scenario: 招聘人接通就说「介绍下你自己」。你上一段工作因公司级裁员结束，这个岗位是你在 LinkedIn 上刷到的。GenLogs 和 Pinpoint 两次你都用这两件事开的场。
scenario_en: The recruiter opens with "tell me about yourself." Your last role ended in a company-wide layoff and you found this posting on LinkedIn — and you opened with exactly those two facts in both GenLogs and Pinpoint.
q: self-intro 的前两句该说什么？
q_en: What belongs in the first two sentences of your self-intro?
options: 先交代来路和处境：「我上一段工作因为公司裁员结束了，最近在 LinkedIn 上刷到你们在招人，看着挺合适，就投了一份简历过来试试。」
先说现在 own 什么再接时间线：「我在 TikTok own 广告投放全链路；此前在 Meta 做 onboarding 平台。」
从第一份工作开始按年份往下讲，把简历每一段的起止时间、职位名称和主要职责依次复述一遍，最后才说到现在。
开场只讲动机：先说你为什么想去创业公司、未来三五年的职业规划，具体做过什么留到对方追问的时候再展开。
options_en: Explain how you got here: "My last role ended in a layoff, I saw your posting on LinkedIn recently, it looked like a fit, so I sent a resume over."
Lead with what you own now, then the timeline: "At TikTok I own the ad campaign flow; before that I built onboarding at Meta."
Walk the resume chronologically from your first job — dates, titles and duties for every stint — and only reach the present at the end.
Open with motivation only: why you want a startup and your three-to-five-year plan, saving what you actually built for follow-ups.
tradeoff: 先说 impact vs 先交代来路：交代来路显得坦诚，代价是最宝贵的前 30 秒被裁员和求职渠道占满。
why: 开场 30 秒决定对方怎么给我贴标签。先说我现在 own 什么系统，再补时间线做证据；裁员和「怎么找到你们」不进开场。
why_en: The first thirty seconds decide how they file me, so I open with the system I own today and use the timeline as evidence behind it.
whenOtherWins: 只有当招聘人第一句就问「你为什么在看新机会」时，才提前说离职情况，而且一句带过就拉回你 own 的东西。
optionMeanings: 用裁员和求职渠道开场。
先给当前 ownership，再补履历。
按年份从头复述整份简历。
开场只谈动机与规划。
optionMeanings_en: Open with the layoff and how you found them.
Lead with current ownership, then the timeline.
Recite the whole resume by year.
Talk only about motivation and plans.
optionDirectness: 内推来的、对方早知情时才无所谓。
对方还不认识你时，先给一个可归类的标签。
对方手上没有简历、要完整履历时才有用。
适合已聊过背景的第二次通话。
optionDirectness_en: Only harmless when a referral already told them the story.
Right when they don't know you yet and need a label fast.
Useful only if they have no resume and want the full record.
Fits a second call where the background is already covered.
optionScenarioImpacts: 开场被裁员定调，能力标签没建立起来。
对方立刻知道你的层级和领域。
信息平铺，重点被时间顺序稀释。
只有意愿没有证据，听着像应届生。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The layoff sets the tone and no capability label lands.
They immediately know your level and your domain.
Everything is flat; chronology dilutes the point.
Intent without evidence sounds like a new grad.

q: self-intro 里描述职责，「some features」要换成什么句式？
q_en: What sentence pattern replaces "some features" when you describe your scope?
text: 自我介绍里「some features」全部删掉，换成三段式：I {{own}} 一个具名系统 — 涵盖它的 {{范围}}，重要性在于 {{影响}}。
text_en: Cut "some features" everywhere and use the three-part line: I {{own}} a named system — it covers this {{scope}}, and it matters because of this {{impact}}.
why: 「some features」既听不出层级也听不出规模。点名系统 + 说清范围 + 给出影响，一句话就把 scope 交代完。
why_en: "Some features" hides both scope and seniority, so name the system, state what it covers, and say why it matters.

scenario: WOP 招聘人 2 分钟里给了五个关键词：数字支付、PSP 集成、税务处理、checkout、tap-to-pay。你只反射一个。你真正做过的是 Meta 的多步骤 onboarding 数据流和 TikTok 的投放校验。
scenario_en: The WOP recruiter gave five keywords in two minutes: digital payments, PSP integrations, tax handling, checkout, tap-to-pay. You will mirror exactly one. What you actually built is Meta’s multi-step onboarding data flow and TikTok campaign validation.
q: 该挑哪个关键词反射回去？
q_en: Which of those keywords should you mirror back?
options: 挑 checkout 的多步流程：我在 Meta 做过从商家输入到后端的多步状态流转，被追问也接得住。
挑听起来最资深的 tax engine，就算自己没真做过，也先把「能扛复杂业务」的印象立起来再说。
五个关键词逐个都呼应一遍，每个说一句，证明你把他讲的每一点都听进去了、也都能接上话。
挑 tap-to-pay：这是最新的技术方向，能表现出你对支付行业前沿趋势的关注度和学习意愿。
options_en: Mirror the multi-step checkout flow: at Meta I built the multi-step state flow from merchant input to backend, so I can take the follow-up.
Mirror the tax engine because it sounds the most senior — even without having built one, it establishes that you handle complex business logic.
Echo all five keywords, one sentence each, to prove you took in every point he made and can speak to all of them.
Mirror tap-to-pay: it is the newest direction and shows how closely you follow payment-industry trends and want to learn.
tradeoff: 挑能接住追问的 vs 挑听起来最资深的：挑资深的开场更响，代价是下一个追问就落在你没做过的东西上。
why: 反射的那个词会立刻变成下一个技术追问。挑我真做过、能往下走两层的，而不是听起来最资深的。
why_en: Whatever keyword I mirror becomes the very next technical follow-up, so I pick the one I actually built and can go two layers deep on.
whenOtherWins: 如果五个关键词你一个都没做过，就反射最接近的那个，并当场说清你做过的是其中哪一段。
optionMeanings: 挑自己真做过的那个词。
挑最显资深的那个词。
五个词全部各回应一句。
挑最新潮的那个词。
optionMeanings_en: Pick the keyword you actually built.
Pick the keyword that sounds most senior.
Answer all five keywords one by one.
Pick the trendiest keyword.
optionDirectness: 你在其中一个方向有真实经历时。
对方明显在担心你级别不够时才有理由。
对方要求你逐条确认理解时才用。
岗位本身就是围绕这项新技术建的时才用。
optionDirectness_en: When you have real experience in one of those areas.
Only justified when they visibly worry you are too junior.
Only when they ask you to confirm each point back.
Only when the role itself is built around that new technology.
optionScenarioImpacts: 追问落在我准备过的那段流程上。
开场很响，第一个追问就穿帮。
开场变成复述清单，一个都没讲深。
话题被引到我没做过的硬件支付上。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The follow-up lands on the flow I have rehearsed.
A loud opening that the first follow-up exposes.
The opening becomes a checklist recital with no depth anywhere.
It steers the conversation to hardware payments I have never built.

scenario: 对方描述完岗位后说「介绍下你自己吧」。你过去两次都从最早的实习按年份往下讲，讲到现在时时间已经用掉一半。
scenario_en: They finish describing the role and say "tell me about yourself." Your last two attempts started at your earliest internship and walked forward by year, burning half the time before reaching the present.
q: self-intro 的四拍该按什么顺序讲？
q_en: In what order should the four beats of the self-intro come?
steps: 点出你想在这个方向深入的地方，把话头交回给对方
先说你现在 own 的系统和它的影响（impact first）
反射对方刚描述的一个具体岗位信号，说明它和你做过的哪件事对上
补一句时间线：此前在哪家公司做了什么，作为证据
why: 不是按年份走，而是 impact 先行、时间线只做证据，然后是连接、最后给方向——对方听完知道我是谁、能证明什么、想去哪。
why_en: Not chronological: impact first, timeline only as evidence, then the connection to their role, and finally the direction I want.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["现在 own 什么 — impact 先行"] --> B["时间线做证据"]
  B --> C["反射一个岗位信号"]
  C --> D["给方向并交回话头"]

scenario: 你的 self-intro 已经说了现在 own 什么、此前在 Meta 做什么，也反射了对方岗位的一个信号。还剩最后一句。
scenario_en: Your self-intro has covered what you own now, what you built at Meta, and one signal mirrored back from their role. One sentence left.
q: self-intro 的最后一句该说什么？
q_en: What should the last sentence of the self-intro do?
options: 再补第三个项目的细节，把简历上还没提到的经历尽量在开场一次讲完，免得后面没有机会说。
说一句「大概就是这些」然后停下来，等对方决定下一步问什么，自己不给任何方向性的信息。
直接问薪资区间和面试还有几轮，趁开场先把最关心的现实问题确认掉，免得后面几轮白花时间。
给方向并交回话头：「我想把支付这条线做深，也想听听这个岗位现在最难的部分是什么。」
options_en: Add a third project in detail so every unmentioned experience gets covered up front, in case there's no chance later.
Say "that's about it" and stop, letting them decide what comes next without offering any direction of your own.
Ask about the salary band and how many rounds remain, settling the practical questions before investing more time.
Give a direction and hand off: "I want to go deep on payments — and I'd like to hear what's hardest in this role right now."
tradeoff: 以方向收口 vs 继续堆项目：多讲一个项目显得内容多，代价是没人接得住，对方还得自己想下一句问什么。
why: 最后一句是交接棒。给一个方向加一个想了解的点，对方顺着往下问的就是我已经准备好的题。
why_en: The closing line is a handoff — give one direction plus one thing you want to know, and their next question lands on ground you already prepared.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方明确说「我想先完整听你的履历」，就把时间花在讲完经历上，方向留到他问 what are you looking for 时再给。
optionMeanings: 再塞一个项目进开场。
自然收尾，不给方向。
开场先谈薪资和流程。
给方向并抛回一个问题。
optionMeanings_en: Squeeze one more project into the opening.
Trail off without giving a direction.
Open with compensation and process.
Give a direction and hand back a question.
optionDirectness: 只有对方明说想听完整履历时才合适。
对方话很密、需要你尽快让出时间时勉强可用。
薪资明显有结构性错配、需要尽早止损时才提前问。
希望对方顺着你的方向提下一个问题时用。
optionDirectness_en: Only when they explicitly asked for the full record.
Barely works when they talk a lot and you must yield time.
Ask early only if a structural pay mismatch needs cutting fast.
Use it when you want their next question on your ground.
optionScenarioImpacts: 开场变长，反射建立的连接被冲淡。
主动权交出去，方向由对方来猜。
还没证明价值就先谈条件，顺序反了。
对方接着问的是你准备过的那块。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The opening drags and the connection you built gets diluted.
You hand over control and let them guess your direction.
Talking terms before proving value inverts the order.
Their follow-up lands on the part you rehearsed.

scenario: 「你为什么离开 TikTok？」在 WOP、GenLogs、Pinpoint、Assembled、Alma、Singular 等场次已经连续 7 次没有结构——Assembled 那次你当场说了「sorry, let me think about that」。
scenario_en: "Why are you leaving TikTok?" has now come out unstructured seven interviews in a row — in the Assembled call you actually said "sorry, let me think about that."
q: 第 7 次之后，真正的修法是什么？
q_en: After the seventh time, what is the actual fix?
options: 写成恰好 3 句（得到了什么 / 还缺什么 / 现在找什么），每天出声练到冷启动零停顿。
临场根据面试官的表情和反应即兴组织语言，保持自然，避免听起来像在背事先写好的稿子。
把完整答案打在纸上放到屏幕旁边，被问到就逐句照着念下来，保证每次说出来的内容完全一致。
把这个问题的答案压成一句「想找一个更能自己做主的机会」，短到几乎不可能说砸，也不给追问的把手。
options_en: Write it as exactly three sentences — what I got, what I'm missing, what I want now — and drill it out loud until it starts cold.
Improvise each time based on the interviewer's reaction, staying natural and avoiding anything that sounds scripted.
Keep the full answer printed next to your screen and read it line by line so every telling is word-for-word identical.
Compress it into one line — "I want a place where I can call more of the shots" — so short it can't go wrong and invites no follow-up.
tradeoff: 写死 3 句练到冷启动 vs 临场即兴：即兴听着自然，代价是已经连着 7 次卡壳，包括当场说「让我想想」。
why: 第 7 次说明缺的不是准备时间，是固定骨架。写死三句、出声练到冷启动，才不会再出现「让我想想」。
why_en: Seven misses means the gap isn't prep time, it's a fixed skeleton — three sentences drilled out loud until they start cold.
whenOtherWins: 只有当对方追一个具体细节（比如「那个项目上线后怎么样」）时，才离开三句骨架临场展开。
optionMeanings: 固定三句骨架并出声练。
每次临场重新组织。
照着稿子逐句念。
压成一句口号式回答。
optionMeanings_en: Fix a three-sentence skeleton and drill it aloud.
Reorganize from scratch every time.
Read a printed script line by line.
Compress it into one slogan.
optionDirectness: 同一个问题反复出问题时的标准解法。
只有这道题本来就答得很稳时才够。
写邮件或书面回复时可以照抄。
只剩十几秒收尾时才用得上。
optionDirectness_en: The standard fix once a question keeps failing.
Only enough if this answer were already reliable.
Fine for a written reply, not a live call.
Only useful when ten seconds remain to close.
optionScenarioImpacts: 第 8 次终于能冷启动说完整。
第 8 次大概率还是同样的卡壳。
念稿的节奏一听就出来，且答非所问。
一句话打发，对方感觉不到你想清楚了。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The eighth time finally comes out whole from a cold start.
The eighth time most likely stalls the same way.
Reading aloud is audible and rarely matches the question.
A one-liner leaves them unsure you've thought it through.

q: 「为什么离开 TikTok」的三句骨架是哪三拍？
q_en: What are the three beats in the "why I'm leaving TikTok" skeleton?
text: 为什么离职 = 三句：① 我在 TikTok 和 Meta {{得到了什么}}（发布、监控、规模化运营的生产直觉）→ ② 我还{{缺什么}}（接近产品决策和客户）→ ③ 我现在{{在找什么}}（端到端 own 一个问题）。
text_en: Why I'm leaving = three sentences: what I {{got}} at TikTok and Meta, what I'm still {{missing}}, and what I'm {{looking for}} now.
why: 三拍是「得到 → 缺 → 找」。有骨架在，被打断也能从任意一拍接回去，不会又退回流水账。
why_en: The arc is got it, missing it, looking for it — with those beats I can be interrupted and still pick the answer back up.

scenario: 答案库里「为什么离职」有三个版本：A 投 <100 人 early-stage、B 投 applied AI 公司、C 投 50-200 人 growth-stage。今天这通电话，对方的产品以 LLM agent 为核心。
scenario_en: Your answer bank has three "why I'm leaving" versions: A for sub-100-person early stage, B for applied-AI companies, C for 50-200-person growth stage. Today's call is with a company whose product is built on LLM agents.
q: 该用哪个版本？
q_en: Which version should you use?
options: 用版本 A：强调想端到端 own 一个问题、从第一个客户信号一直到上线看到结果，这条对任何比大厂小的公司都成立，也最好说。
用版本 C：强调把大厂的可靠性和发布流程带进一个架构决策还在制定中的环境，并参与塑造这些决策。
三个版本各说一小段，把自己想要的东西一次说全，让对方从里面自己挑他们最在意的那一条。
用版本 B：从 Meta 给 AI agent 喂业务数据的那层切入，说想参与 AI 系统本身的设计与评估。
options_en: Use version A: end-to-end ownership of a problem from the first customer signal all the way to launch — true of any company smaller than big tech, and the easiest to deliver.
Use version C: bring big-company reliability and rollout process into an environment where architecture decisions are still open to shape.
Give a slice of all three so everything you want is on the table and they can pick whichever matters most to them.
Use version B: start from the Meta layer that fed business data to the AI agent, and say you want inside the design and evaluation of the AI system itself.
tradeoff: 按公司类型选版本 vs 一套通吃：通吃省准备，代价是对 applied AI 公司说不出你离 AI 最近的那段经历。
why: 版本要对上对方的产品核心。对做 LLM agent 的公司，Meta 那段 onboarding 是我离 AI 最近的经历，不用等于浪费。
why_en: Match the version to their product core — for an LLM-agent company, the Meta onboarding layer is the closest I've been to AI and leaving it out wastes it.
whenOtherWins: 如果这家做的是 AI 之外的业务（支付、物流、B2B 工作流），版本 B 反而跑题，该退回 A 或 C。
optionMeanings: 端到端 ownership 版本。
把大厂经验带进扩张期版本。
三个版本混着说一遍。
回到 AI 系统本身的版本。
optionMeanings_en: The end-to-end ownership version.
The bring-big-company-rigor-to-growth version.
A blend of all three versions.
The go-back-into-the-AI-system version.
optionDirectness: 面对 0-1 阶段的小团队时最贴。
面对已有客户、正在扩张的团队时最贴。
任何单场面试都不该这么用。
对方产品核心就是模型或 agent 时最贴。
optionDirectness_en: Best against a 0-to-1 team still finding the product.
Best against a team with customers and a scaling problem.
Never the right move inside a single interview.
Best when the model or agent is their product core.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对，但没用上你唯一的 AI 经历。
扩张期语言对上不了 agent 产品的痛点。
三段并列等于没有立场，听着像在挑工作。
把最相关的一段经历放到了答案正中间。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Not wrong, but it leaves your only AI experience unused.
Scaling language doesn't touch what an agent product hurts from.
Three answers at once reads as shopping rather than choosing.
It puts your most relevant experience at the center.

q: 「为什么离职」的 A/B/C 三个版本各对应什么类型的公司？
q_en: Which company type does each of the A/B/C "why I'm leaving" versions target?
text: 版本 A → {{early-stage}}（<100 人、产品还在 0-1）；版本 B → {{applied AI}}（产品以 LLM/agent 为核心）；版本 C → {{growth-stage}}（50-200 人、已有客户开始扩张）。
text_en: Version A → {{early-stage}} (under 100 people, still 0-to-1); version B → {{applied AI}} (LLM or agent is the product); version C → {{growth-stage}} (50-200 people, customers already onboard).
why: 会前十分钟先判断公司类型再挑版本，判断依据是人数和产品阶段，不是行业标签。
why_en: Ten minutes before the call I classify the company by headcount and product stage, not by industry label, and pick the matching version.

scenario: 面试官问「你为什么离开 TikTok？」你答到一半顺势接上「所以我很想加入你们，因为你们做的东西……」，两个问题揉成了一段。
scenario_en: Asked "why are you leaving TikTok?", you slid halfway through into "...which is why I'd love to join you, because what you're building..." — merging two questions into one answer.
q: 这两题为什么必须分开答？
q_en: Why do these two questions have to stay separate?
options: 揉在一起没问题，本来就是同一件事的两面，一次说完还能省时间、显得逻辑连贯、不啰嗦。
分开答：离职那题只讲我缺什么，「为什么来这家」留到对方问，那时才点名他们的产品做连接。
分开答是因为面试官按题打分，混答会让评分表上有一栏空着，最后被算成没有回答这道题。
应该反过来：先讲为什么来这家，再顺带解释离职，用对这家公司的热情把离职话题盖过去。
options_en: Merging is fine — they're two sides of one thing, and covering both at once saves time and sounds coherent.
Keep them apart: the leaving answer only says what I'm missing, and why-this-company waits until they ask, so I can name their product then.
Keep them apart because interviewers score per question, and a merged answer leaves a blank row that counts as unanswered.
Do the reverse: lead with why this company and fold the leaving reason in, letting enthusiasm cover the departure topic.
tradeoff: 分开答 vs 揉成一段：揉着说省一次开口，代价是三句骨架被冲散，两边的落点都讲不深。
why: 离职那题的落点是「我缺什么」，why this company 的落点是「你们有什么」。合在一起，两个落点互相稀释。
why_en: The leaving answer lands on what I'm missing and why-this-company lands on what they have, so merging them dilutes both landings.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方直接问「为什么离开现在的公司来我们这」，那就是一题两问，这时才用一句话把两边接起来。
optionMeanings: 合并成一段一次讲完。
两题各自独立、各有落点。
以评分表机制为由分开。
先讲来意再补离职原因。
optionMeanings_en: Merge them into one continuous answer.
Keep two answers with two distinct landings.
Separate them because of scoring mechanics.
Lead with the attraction and tuck the exit in after.
optionDirectness: 对方一句话把两题一起问出来时才成立。
两题分别被问出来时的默认做法。
机制猜测；换个面试官就不成立。
离职原因确实敏感、想快速带过时的权宜。
optionDirectness_en: Only holds when they literally ask both in one breath.
The default whenever the two questions arrive separately.
A guess about scoring; a different interviewer breaks it.
A stopgap when the exit reason is genuinely sensitive.
optionScenarioImpacts: 三句骨架讲到一半就被自己岔断。
离职讲完整，公司理由留在最有效的位置。
理由是编的机制，真被追问会露馅。
热情盖不住空缺，对方还会把离职题问回来。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You derail your own three-sentence arc halfway through.
The exit lands whole and the company reason keeps its best slot.
The reasoning is invented and collapses under a follow-up.
Enthusiasm doesn't cover the gap; they ask the exit question again.

q: 「Why now」和「为什么离职」怎么分工，该说哪三件事？
q_en: How does "why now" differ from "why are you leaving," and which three things does it cover?
text: Why now 单独准备，说三件：我在 TikTok 待了{{多久}}、交付了{{哪些具体项目}}（Promotion Day、GM Max）、以及为什么{{现在}}是带着这个基础去下一站的时机。
text_en: Prepare "why now" separately and cover three things: {{how long}} I've been at TikTok, {{which projects}} I shipped, and why {{now}} is the right moment to take that foundation somewhere else.
why: 离职题讲的是缺口，why now 讲的是时机——待了多久、交付了什么、所以现在收得住。两题分开背。
why_en: The leaving answer is about the gap and why-now is about timing — how long, what shipped, and why the chapter closes cleanly here.

scenario: GenLogs 那次「为什么离职」，你把「end to end」重复了 4 次，中间没有转折也没有递进，整段听下来是同一个词的四种说法。
scenario_en: In the GenLogs call your "why I'm leaving" repeated "end to end" four times with no turn and no build — four phrasings of one word.
q: 这段回答的问题出在哪、怎么改？
q_en: What's actually wrong with that answer, and how do you fix it?
options: 缺弧线：四次「end to end」全是「我想要什么」，没有「我得到了什么」和「我还缺什么」这两拍。
用词太单调，换成 autonomy、full-stack、独立负责这些近义词轮流说，内容听起来就丰富了。
整段太短了，应该再举两个项目例子把它撑到一分半，信息量上去之后自然就有说服力了。
关键词选错了，「end to end」太抽象，应该整段换成「更接近客户痛点」这个说法反复强调。
options_en: It has no arc: all four "end to end"s are what I want, with no beat for what I got and what I'm missing.
The wording is monotonous — rotate through autonomy, full-stack and owning it yourself and it will sound much richer.
It's too short — add two more project examples to stretch it to ninety seconds and the volume will carry it.
The keyword is wrong — "end to end" is too abstract, so repeat "closer to customer pain" throughout instead.
tradeoff: 补齐三拍 vs 换同义词：换词让句子不重复，代价是整段仍然只有「我想要」一种信息。
why: 重复一个词不等于有结构。一段合格的回答里要出现三种不同信息：得到了什么、缺什么、现在找什么。
why_en: Repeating one phrase is not structure — a working answer carries three different kinds of information, not one said four ways.
optionMeanings: 问题是缺三拍中的两拍。
问题是词汇重复。
问题是篇幅不够。
问题是关键词选错。
optionMeanings_en: The problem is two missing beats.
The problem is repeated vocabulary.
The problem is insufficient length.
The problem is the wrong keyword.
optionDirectness: 整段只表达了一种诉求时的诊断。
结构已经完整、只是措辞单调时才对。
回答确实短到只有一句时才对。
关键词与对方业务完全无关时才对。
optionDirectness_en: The right diagnosis when the whole answer expresses one wish.
Only right if the structure is already complete and dull.
Only right if the answer really is a single sentence.
Only right when the keyword misses their business entirely.
optionScenarioImpacts: 补上前两拍，这段立刻有了因果。
换四个词说同一件事，信息量没变。
拉长到九十秒，重复也跟着变长。
换个词继续重复，还是一拍到底。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Adding the first two beats gives the answer cause and effect.
Four synonyms for one idea carry the same information.
Stretching to ninety seconds just stretches the repetition.
A new keyword repeated is still a single beat.

scenario: 你已经在不同场次说过两个方向：Inventing VC 那次是「infra AI 平台与可靠性」，WOP、Assembled、Pinpoint 是「端到端 ownership、更接近客户」。现在要挑一条以后只说它。
scenario_en: You have already given two directions in different calls: infrastructure AI platform and reliability at Inventing VC, and end-to-end ownership closer to the customer at WOP, Assembled and Pinpoint. Now you have to keep exactly one.
q: 该按什么依据挑出留下的那一条？
q_en: On what basis do you choose which direction to keep?
options: 挑听起来更资深的那条：infra 和可靠性在大厂语境里更像高级工程师的活，定级时也许更占便宜。
挑简历上字面证据更多的那条：哪条方向在简历里能找到更多关键词就留哪条，改起来也最省事。
先不挑：两条都留着，等某一家公司明确表态更看重哪一条时，再顺着他们的偏好把方向定下来。
挑实际反馈更好、且对得上你正在投的岗位类型的那条——产品向的端到端 ownership 就是它。
options_en: Keep whichever sounds more senior: infra and reliability read as higher-level work in big-tech language and may help at level-setting.
Keep whichever has more literal evidence on the resume, since the direction with more matching keywords is the cheapest to support.
Do not choose yet: hold both and let the first company that states a preference decide the direction for you.
Keep the one that has drawn better real responses and matches the roles you are applying to — the product-side end-to-end ownership line.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["两个方向都说出去了"] --> B["依据一 — 哪条拿到的实际反馈更好"]
  A --> C["依据二 — 我正在投哪一类岗位"]
  B --> D["留下产品向端到端 ownership"]
  C --> D
  D --> E["简历与故事按这一条重排"]
tradeoff: 按实际反馈挑 vs 按听起来资深挑：挑资深的短期定级也许好看，代价是我拿不出对应的故障、容量和可靠性数字。
why: 依据是「哪条是真的、我投的又是哪类岗位」，不是哪条听着更高级。产品向那条拿到的回应更好，就留它。
why_en: Choose by which direction is actually true and matches the roles I am applying to, not by which sounds more senior — the product line has drawn the better responses.
whenOtherWins: 如果我把投递重心整体切到平台/基础设施岗位，那就该改留 infra 那条——但简历和故事要跟着一起重排。
optionMeanings: 按听起来的资深程度挑。
按简历关键词数量挑。
推迟决定，让对方来定。
按真实反馈和投递方向挑。
optionMeanings_en: Choose by which sounds more senior.
Choose by which has more resume keywords.
Defer the decision and let them choose.
Choose by real responses and where you are applying.
optionDirectness: 只有你确实打算补齐可靠性经历时才成立。
简历本来就写得很准时才勉强够用。
你自己确实还在两条路之间摇摆时才诚实。
你已经积累了几十场反馈、能看出规律时。
optionDirectness_en: Only valid if you genuinely intend to build the reliability record.
Barely enough when the resume was already written accurately.
Honest only if you truly are still torn between the two paths.
Right once you have dozens of calls worth of signal to read.
optionScenarioImpacts: 定级也许好看，深挖时讲不出故障案例。
关键词多不代表故事强，追问会露底。
每家给一个版本，漂移问题原封不动。
方向和证据对齐，以后每场都能重复。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It may read as senior until a deep dive asks for an incident story.
More keywords is not a stronger story, and probing exposes the gap.
Each company gets its own version and the drift problem stays.
Direction and evidence line up, so every future call repeats it.

scenario: 你要在「平台/基础设施工程」和「产品工程」之间选一条对外统一的叙事线。两条线在面试里被问的问题、要的证据都不一样。
scenario_en: You have to pick one public narrative line — platform/infrastructure engineering or product engineering. The two get asked different questions and demand different evidence.
q: 这两条叙事线的根本区别落在哪个维度？
q_en: On which dimension do these two narrative lines actually differ?
options: 落在公司规模上：平台线只存在于大厂、产品线只存在于创业公司，挑公司规模就等于替你选好了线。
落在技术栈上：平台线写 Go 和 Kubernetes、产品线写 React 和 TypeScript，语言选择决定你属于哪条线。
落在职级上：平台线更容易被评成资深、产品线偏初级，所以一律往平台线靠会拿到更高的定级。
落在你服务谁：平台线的客户是内部工程师、用可靠性衡量；产品线的客户是终端用户、用采纳衡量。
options_en: Company size: platform work only exists in big tech and product work only in startups, so picking a size picks your line.
Tech stack: platform means Go and Kubernetes, product means React and TypeScript, and the language decides which line you're on.
Level: platform work is read as more senior and product work as junior, so leaning platform gets you a higher offer level.
Who you serve: platform serves internal engineers and is measured by reliability; product serves end users and is measured by adoption.
tradeoff: 平台线 vs 产品线：平台线要的是可靠性数字，产品线要的是客户影响；同一段经历没法同时当两边最强的证据。
why: 区别在服务对象和衡量指标，不在公司大小或语言。选一条，再把 TikTok/Meta 的经历按那条线重排证据。
why_en: The split is who you serve and how you're measured, not company size or language, so pick one line and re-rank your evidence for it.
optionMeanings: 按公司规模划分两条线。
按编程语言划分两条线。
按职级高低划分两条线。
按服务对象与指标划分。
optionMeanings_en: Split the lines by company size.
Split the lines by programming language.
Split the lines by seniority level.
Split by who you serve and how you're measured.
optionDirectness: 只在你只考虑一种规模的公司时勉强成立。
描述现象可以，用来定叙事线会选错。
薪资谈判里的传闻，不是叙事线的分界。
决定面试官会问你要哪一类证据。
optionDirectness_en: Barely holds if you only ever target one company size.
Fine as an observation, wrong as a way to choose a line.
Compensation folklore, not a boundary between narratives.
It decides which kind of evidence the interviewer asks for.
optionScenarioImpacts: 大厂也有产品岗，这条线立刻自相矛盾。
你两种语言都写过，划不出线来。
按传闻选方向，最后讲不出对应的故事。
选定后就知道该准备哪一类故事和数字。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Big tech has product roles too, so the rule contradicts itself.
You've written both stacks, so it draws no line at all.
Choosing by folklore leaves you without matching stories.
Once chosen, you know which stories and numbers to prepare.

scenario: Playground 那次「为什么选这家」答得最好：你找到了 childcare 的具体产品域（计费、注册、报表），点了名，再说这种直接的客户影响吸引你。
scenario_en: The Playground call produced your best "why this company": you found the concrete product domain — childcare billing, registration, reporting — named it out loud, then said why that direct customer impact appeals to you.
q: 把「为什么选这家公司」的四步公式排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four steps of the "why this company" formula in order.
steps: 点名说出来：「你们做的是 childcare 的计费、注册和报表」
会前研究官网和产品页，找出他们具体的产品域
连回你做过的东西，说明你已经具备了做这件事的哪一半
说明这种客户影响为什么打动你
why: 研究 → 点名 → 说客户影响为什么打动我 → 连回我做过的。少了点名那一步，答案就退回成通用创业好话。
why_en: Research it, name it out loud, say why that customer impact moves me, then connect it to what I've already built — skip the naming step and it collapses into generic startup praise.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["会前研究官网与产品页"] --> B["点名具体产品域"]
  B --> C["说明客户影响为何打动我"]
  C --> D["连回我做过的经历"]

scenario: Eclipse Performance 的联创 Johnny 讲了：运动表现可穿戴 sleeve、他自己在用 Oura Ring 和 Apple Watch、另一位联创是半职业足球运动员。你回答的是「focus on the performance and building things at the system level」。
scenario_en: Eclipse's co-founder described a sports-performance wearable sleeve, said he uses an Oura Ring and Apple Watch himself, and that his co-founder played semi-pro soccer. You answered "focus on the performance and building things at the system level."
q: 这句回答错在哪、该换成什么？
q_en: What's wrong with that answer and what replaces it?
options: 错在太谦虚了，应该强调自己在大厂做过更复杂的系统，一个可穿戴设备的后端对你来说并不算难。
错在零产品连接——该说：消费级手环给的数据和运动员真正要的之间有差距，你们用硬件加软件补这个差距。
错在没提融资——应该先恭喜他们拿到 150 万美元，说明你看好这个赛道的商业前景和长期空间。
错在说得太短，应该把「system level」展开讲三分钟，把你的架构能力完整铺开给两位创始人听。
options_en: It's too modest — you should stress that you've built more complex systems in big tech and a wearable backend isn't hard for you.
It has zero product connection — say instead that consumer trackers leave a gap versus what athletes need, and they close it with hardware plus software.
It skips the funding — congratulate them on the $1.5M raise and show you believe in the market's commercial upside.
It's too short — expand "system level" into three minutes and lay out your full architecture capability for both founders.
tradeoff: 点名产品缺口 vs 说技术层级：技术层级到哪家都能说，代价是 18 分钟的创始人电话里，对方听不出你为什么来找他们。
why: 「system level」是技术词，不是产品连接。会前 5 分钟看官网就能说出他们在补的那道缺口：消费级数据和运动员需求之间。
why_en: "System level" is a technical word, not a product connection — five minutes on their site would have told me the gap they close between consumer data and what athletes need.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方是纯技术面试官、明确问你想做什么层级的工程，那时才谈系统层级和架构偏好。
optionMeanings: 把问题归为姿态太低。
把问题归为缺产品连接。
把问题归为没谈商业面。
把问题归为讲得不够长。
optionMeanings_en: Blames the answer for being too modest.
Blames it for having no product connection.
Blames it for skipping the business side.
Blames it for being too short.
optionDirectness: 对方明确怀疑你能力不够时才该这么答。
创始人刚描述完产品和使用场景时该这么答。
对方是投资人、在评估市场时才该这么答。
面试官明确要求展开架构细节时才该这么答。

Right after a founder has described the product and its users.
Only when the other side is an investor sizing the market.
Only when the interviewer explicitly asks for architecture depth.
optionScenarioImpacts: 把一次产品对话拧成了能力辩护。
接住了他刚说的产品缺口，连接成立。
创始人要的是同路人，不是看好行情的人。
讲更久也还是没提到 sleeve 和运动员。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Turns a product conversation into a defence of your ability.
Catches the gap he just described, and the connection lands.
Founders want a fellow believer, not a market bull.

scenario: Alma 做移民方向的 AI 产品，招聘人用了「helping people navigate high-stakes immigration journeys」这句话。你本人正在走绿卡流程（AOS 调整身份、持 EAD），当时只回了「yeah, it sounds interesting」。
scenario_en: Alma builds AI for immigration; the recruiter used the phrase "helping people navigate high-stakes immigration journeys." You are going through the green-card process yourself (adjustment of status, holding an EAD) and answered only "yeah, it sounds interesting."
q: 产品正好是你自己在经历的事，这时该说什么？
q_en: Their product is literally your own life right now — what do you say?
options: 立刻说出来：我本人正在走绿卡流程，亲身体验过这套系统多不透明，把它做清楚对我不是抽象的事。
保持职业距离、完全不谈个人身份状况，避免签证话题影响对方对雇佣成本和流程复杂度的判断。
先说「sounds interesting」，等对方主动问到你的身份状态时，再顺势提一句你在走绿卡流程这件事。
把话题转到技术方案上，说移民材料审核很适合用文档抽取和检索来做，借机展示你对技术选型的判断。
options_en: Say it right away: I'm going through the green-card process myself, I know firsthand how opaque it is, and making it clearer isn't abstract to me.
Keep professional distance and never raise your immigration status, so visa questions don't shape their view of hiring cost and complexity.
Say "sounds interesting" first and only mention the green-card process later, if and when they ask about your status themselves.
Pivot to the technical side — immigration paperwork suits document extraction and retrieval — and show your judgment on architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调整身份：人在美国境内直接把当前签证身份转成永久居民（绿卡）的流程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adjustment of Status is the process of changing to permanent resident status from inside the United States.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工作许可卡：在绿卡审批期间合法工作的临时凭证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Employment Authorization Document is the temporary card that lets you work legally while a green card is pending.

tradeoff: 立刻说出亲身经历 vs 保持职业距离：保持距离显得专业，代价是丢掉一个别人编不出来的「为什么是我」。
why: 亲身经历是别人抄不走的 why-this-company。产品和我的生活重叠时当场说出来，比任何精心设计的答案都有力。
why_en: Lived experience is a why-this-company nobody else can copy, so when their product overlaps my own life I say it in the moment.
whenOtherWins: 如果个人经历会牵出你这轮不想谈的事（比如需要担保的时间表），可以只说「我熟悉这个流程」，不展开细节。

Swap the topic for an architecture pitch.

Use it in a purely technical round before motivation comes up.

scenario: GenLogs 的招聘人问「你对我们了解多少？」你把官网首页的产品介绍复述了一遍，没有加任何自己的看法。
scenario_en: The GenLogs recruiter asked "what do you know about us?" and you recited the homepage product blurb without adding a single opinion of your own.
q: 这类问题的正确结构是什么？
q_en: What structure does this question actually want?
options: 把官网首页、About 页和最近一篇新闻稿的内容尽量完整复述出来，信息越全越能证明你做过功课。
坦白说了解不多，请对方先完整介绍一遍公司，这样既诚实又能拿到最准确的一手信息再来回应。
一句话说他们做什么 → 一个你真感兴趣的做法 → 一个连回你经验的点，最后用一个问题收尾。
跳过产品，直接谈你对这个行业整体的判断和未来三年趋势，展示你的视野比首页信息更有价值。
options_en: Recite the homepage, the About page and the latest press release as completely as you can — more coverage proves more homework.
Admit you don't know much and ask them to walk you through the company, which is honest and gets you accurate first-hand information.
One line on what they do, one thing about their approach that genuinely interests you, one link to your experience, then close with a question.
Skip the product and give your read on the industry and the next three years, showing a perspective worth more than the homepage.
tradeoff: 带观点的三段式 vs 复述首页：复述安全，代价是听起来像刚刚才打开官网。
why: 纯产品描述没有观点，等于只读了首页。要给一个我真感兴趣的点、一个和我经历的连接，再用问题把话头交回去。
why_en: A pure product description carries no opinion, so I add the thing that genuinely interests me, one link to my own work, and a question to hand back.
whenOtherWins: 如果这是 cold outreach、对方自己都还没介绍公司，那就诚实说「我看了官网，想先听你讲讲」，再用一个具体问题接住。

scenario: Apple 下一轮要重写「why Apple」。这个组是 Commerce Accounts / pre-buy：账户创建与更新、换国家、成年验证、payment-on-file、支付栈校验、购买流程被打断后的恢复。
scenario_en: You're rewriting "why Apple" for the next round. The team is Commerce Accounts / pre-buy: account create and update, country change, adult verification, payment-on-file, payment-stack checks, and recovering an interrupted buy flow.
q: 「why Apple」该怎么写？
q_en: How should "why Apple" be written?
options: 说你是多年的 Apple 用户、日常都在用他们的设备和服务，也认同他们对产品质量和细节的长期追求。
点名这个组的问题：购买流程被打断后的状态恢复和支付栈校验，正是我在 TikTok 投放校验里做的正确性护栏。
说 Apple 的品牌和用户规模能让你的工作直接影响到几亿人，这是在任何一家创业公司都拿不到的量级和曝光度。
说你想学习 Apple 内部的工程文化和代码评审流程，把这些大厂最佳实践沉淀成自己长期的技术判断力。
options_en: Say you've been an Apple user for years, you live on their devices and services, and you share their long-term commitment to quality.
Name this team's problem: recovering an interrupted buy flow and validating the payment stack is exactly the correctness guardrail work I did on TikTok campaign validation.
Say Apple's brand and user base let your work reach hundreds of millions — a scale and visibility no startup can offer.
Say you want to learn Apple's engineering culture and code-review process and turn those big-company practices into lasting judgment.
tradeoff: 点名团队问题域 vs 说品牌与用户身份：用户身份人人都能说，代价是听不出你为什么要来这个组、而不是 Apple 的任何一个组。
why: 公司级的赞美对每个组都成立。点名 pre-buy 的真实问题——被打断的购买流程要能恢复——再 bridge 到我做过的校验护栏。
why_en: Company-level praise fits every team, so I name this team's real problem, interrupted buy flows that must recover, and bridge it to the validation guardrails I built.
whenOtherWins: 如果这一轮的面试官来自别的组、只做通用筛选，就先给一句公司层面的理由，再反问他们组具体在做什么。
optionMeanings: 以用户身份和品牌认同作答。
点名该组问题并 bridge 到自己经历。
以规模和影响人数作答。
以学习大厂流程作答。
optionMeanings_en: Answer from user identity and brand affinity.
Name the team's problem and bridge to your own work.
Answer from scale and number of users reached.
Answer from wanting to learn big-company process.

已经知道具体组和它负责什么时的默认答法。
对方在推销岗位吸引力、你顺着接时可用。
你确实是转行或初级、把学习当卖点时才用。

The default once you know the team and what it owns.
Works when they're selling the role and you're echoing back.
Only when you're genuinely junior and learning is the pitch.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对 Apple 的任何一个组都成立，等于没答。
面试官听到你研究过他们真正在解的问题。
谈的是公司资产，不是你能接手的活。
把自己放在索取方，没说你能带来什么。

They hear that you studied the problem they actually solve.

scenario: 简历上 Gemini 约 4 个月、Meta 1 年 3 个月、TikTok 1 年。Apple 那轮面试官就这件事追问了三次，因为你前两次的答案都是「想成长」「想去更大规模」。
scenario_en: Your resume shows Gemini about 4 months, Meta 1 year 3 months, TikTok 1 year. The Apple interviewer probed it three separate times because your first two answers were "growth" and "larger scale."
q: 第一次被问到时该怎么答？
q_en: How should you answer the very first time it comes up?
options: 只解释最近一次跳槽，前面两段等对方追问了再说，每次少说一点可以降低这个话题的存在感。
强调每一段都学到很多、成长得很快，用积极的态度把这个话题整体带过去，不逐段解释每次离开的具体原因和背景。
反问面试官为什么关心在职时间的长短，说明你更看重每段经历真实的产出而不是任期本身。
一次讲完：先给最强的正当理由（Meta 是公司级裁员），再给每次跳槽一个具体的「奔向什么」，20 秒收口。
options_en: Explain only the most recent move and leave the earlier two until they probe, since saying less each time keeps the topic small.
Stress that you learned a lot and grew fast in each stint, carrying the whole topic on tone instead of giving the reason and context for each exit.
Ask the interviewer why tenure length matters to them and argue that output per stint counts more than time served.
Do it in one pass: lead with the hardest legitimate reason (Meta was a company-wide layoff), then one concrete "toward what" per move, closing in twenty seconds.
tradeoff: 一次讲完 vs 挤牙膏：挤牙膏每次都短，代价是对方要追问三次，每追一次都在确认「这里有问题」。
why: 被追问三次说明答案不完整。先给最硬的事实，再给每段一个「奔向什么」，一口气讲完就没有第二次追问。
why_en: Three probes means the answer was incomplete, so I lead with the hardest fact and give one concrete destination per move in a single pass.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方只问了其中一段（「Gemini 为什么只待了四个月」），就只答那一段，别把三段全倒出来。
optionMeanings: 一次只解释一段。
用积极态度整体带过。
把问题反问回去。
一次给完理由和去向。
optionMeanings_en: Explain one stint at a time.
Carry the whole topic on positive tone.
Turn the question back on them.
Give the reason and every destination at once.
optionDirectness: 对方明确只关心最近这一段时才够。
简历上只有一段短任期时勉强成立。
对方问法带明显偏见、需要划边界时才用。
简历上有三段短任期、一眼可见时的默认。
optionDirectness_en: Enough only when they care about the most recent move alone.
Barely holds when there is just one short stint on the page.
Use it only if the question itself was openly biased.
The default when three short stints are visible at a glance.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方追第二次、第三次，疑虑越滚越大。
态度积极但没有事实，追问照旧。
把一个事实问题变成了对立场面。

scenario: 面试官盯着简历上三段短任期问「能讲讲这些跳动吗？」你要在 20 秒内一次讲完。
scenario_en: The interviewer looks at three short stints and asks "can you walk me through these moves?" You have twenty seconds to do it in one pass.
q: 把 20 秒短任期回答的四拍排成正确顺序。
q_en: Order the four beats of the twenty-second short-tenure answer.
steps: 给每一次跳槽一个具体的「奔向什么」，一段一句
先说最强的正当理由：Meta 那次是公司级裁员，不是我的选择
停下来，把话头交回去，不再自己往下补充
收口到现在：所以我现在找的是能待下去、能做深的地方
why: 最硬的事实放最前面，再逐段给「奔向什么」，收口到现在要什么，然后停。停不住就会变成第二次解释。
why_en: Hardest fact first, one destination per move, land on what I want now, and then stop — if I keep talking it becomes a second round of explaining.

q: 三段经历各自的「奔向什么」分别是哪一句？
q_en: What is the one-line "toward what" for each of the three stints?
text: 每次跳槽给一个具体的奔向：Gemini 做 {{Excel 自动化}} → Meta 做{{生产规模的 AI onboarding}} → TikTok 拿到{{端到端 ownership}}；Meta 那段的离开理由是公司级裁员，不是我的选择。
text_en: One concrete destination per move: Gemini for {{Excel automation}}, Meta for {{production-scale AI onboarding}}, TikTok for {{end-to-end ownership}} — and the Meta exit was a company-wide layoff, not my choice.
why: 「想成长」「想去更大规模」对每一段都成立，等于没说。每段配一个只属于那段的去向，追问就停了。
why_en: "Growth" and "bigger scale" fit every stint and therefore say nothing, so each move gets a destination that only belongs to it.

scenario: 简历上三段短任期一眼可见。面试官还没提这件事，你的 self-intro 也快讲完了。
scenario_en: Three short stints are visible at a glance on your resume. The interviewer hasn't raised it and your self-intro is nearly done.
q: 要不要主动把短任期讲了？
q_en: Should you bring the short tenures up yourself?
options: 不主动提，等对方问再答——没被问就说明对方不在意，主动提反而等于自己把短板翻出来。
在时间线那一拍里顺手一句带过（「Meta 那次是公司级裁员」），把解释权握在自己手上。
主动展开讲三分钟，把每段的来龙去脉、团队情况和离职过程都完整交代清楚，杜绝任何疑问。
在简历上把每段离职原因写成一行小字，面试里完全不用口头提，把宝贵的通话时间留给项目。
options_en: Don't raise it — if they didn't ask, they don't care, and volunteering it just digs up your own weak spot.
Slip one clause into the timeline beat ("Meta was a company-wide layoff") so you keep control of the framing.
Volunteer three full minutes covering the background, team situation and exit process of every stint so no doubt survives.
Put a one-line reason under each role on the resume and never mention it aloud, saving call time for projects.
tradeoff: 顺手一句带过 vs 等对方问：等着被问显得低调，代价是话题由对方带着怀疑开场，你只能被动解释。
why: 简历摆在那里，问题一定会来。在时间线里一句带过，是我定调；等他问，就变成他带着疑问审我。
why_en: The resume is right there so the question is coming, and one clause inside my own timeline lets me set the frame instead of defending it.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方明确说过「简历我看过、没什么问题」，就不用再翻出来，把时间留给项目内容。
optionMeanings: 完全等对方发问。
在时间线里一句带过。
主动展开完整解释。
只写在简历上不口头提。
optionMeanings_en: Wait entirely for them to ask.
Slip one clause into the timeline.
Volunteer a full explanation.
Put it on paper and never say it aloud.
optionDirectness: 只有一段短任期、且不显眼时才安全。
任期问题一眼可见、必然会被问时的默认。
对方已经明确表示这是主要顾虑时才值得。
书面申请阶段有用，通话里不解决问题。

optionScenarioImpacts_en: They open the topic and you start from defence.
One clause sets the frame and later questions stay inside it.

scenario: 被问「你本科是建筑智能与自动化，怎么转到软件的？」你当时的版本是：「中国的建筑市场变差了，所以找那种工作不容易。」
scenario_en: Asked "your degree was building intelligence and automation — how did you end up in software?", your version was "the architecture market in China got worse, so that job was hard to find."
q: 这个版本该怎么改写？
q_en: How should that version be rewritten?
options: 补充当时的行业数据和就业率，用客观事实证明你的判断是理性的，而不是随手换了一个赛道。
淡化本科背景，直接从第一份软件工作讲起，尽量不让面试官注意到你不是计算机科班出身的。
改成主动选择：专业本就在物理系统和软件控制的交叉点上，软件一直是我最感兴趣的一半，毕业时我主动选了这边。
强调转型过程很辛苦、业余自学了大量内容，用你付出的代价来证明对软件这条路的决心和长期投入，让对方放心。
options_en: Add industry data and employment rates to prove the decision was rational rather than a casual switch of tracks.
Play down the degree and start from your first software job so the interviewer never notices the non-CS background.
Reframe it as an active choice: the degree sat at the intersection of physical systems and software control, software was always the half I cared about, and I chose it deliberately on graduating.
Stress how hard the transition was and how much you self-taught, using the cost you paid to prove long-term commitment to software and reassure them.
tradeoff: 主动选择 vs 市场变差：说市场变差是真话且好讲，代价是听起来软件只是当年没别的选项时的默认项。
why: 「市场变差所以做软件」把我说成被动接盘。同一段事实换成「专业本就在交叉点、我主动选了软件」，就是有目的的路径。
why_en: Blaming the market makes software sound like a fallback, while the same facts framed as an intersection I deliberately chose read as a deliberate path.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方直接追问当年的就业环境，可以承认市场因素，但落点仍要回到「我主动选了软件」，不停在环境上。
optionMeanings: 为被动版本补上数据支撑。
回避本科背景不谈。
把同一段事实改成主动选择。
用付出的代价证明决心。
optionMeanings_en: Back the passive version with data.
Avoid the degree topic altogether.
Reframe the same facts as an active choice.
Prove commitment through the cost you paid.
optionDirectness: 对方质疑你判断草率、要证据时才用。
背景与岗位完全无关、时间又很紧时才用。
对方在判断这次转型是不是想清楚了的时候用。
对方担心你会不会又转回去时可以补一句。
optionDirectness_en: Use it only when they doubt the decision was considered.
Use it only if the background is irrelevant and time is short.
Use it when they're judging whether the pivot was thought through.
A useful add-on if they fear you'll pivot back again.
optionScenarioImpacts: 数据再全，故事仍然是被环境推着走。
回避会让面试官自己去补最坏的解释。
同样的经历读起来变成有意图的路径。
辛苦不等于合适，还是没说为什么是软件。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: More data still leaves a story driven by circumstance.
Avoidance lets the interviewer fill the gap with the worst reading.
The same history now reads as an intentional path.
Effort isn't fit; it still doesn't say why software.

q: 机械/建筑 → 软件的转型叙事，四拍分别是什么？
q_en: What are the four beats of the mechanical-to-software pivot story?
text: 转型叙事：① 我的专业在{{物理系统和软件控制}}的交叉点上 → ② 软件一直是我最感兴趣的那一半 → ③ 毕业时我{{主动选择}}深入软件 → ④ 第一份工作进创业公司{{从零做起}}。
text_en: The pivot story: my degree sat at the intersection of {{physical systems and software control}}; software was always the half I cared about; on graduating I {{actively chose}} to go deep in software; and my first job was {{building from scratch}} at a startup.
why: 把「找不到工作」换成「交叉点 + 主动选择 + 从零做起」。事实没变，落点从妥协变成有意图的路径。
why_en: Swap "couldn't find work" for intersection, deliberate choice, and building from scratch — same facts, but the landing moves from compromise to intent.

scenario: Pinpoint 的招聘人问「你对什么样的工作感兴趣 / 你接下来想做什么？」你在回答里列了 React、GraphQL、SQL。
scenario_en: The Pinpoint recruiter asked "what kind of work are you interested in / what are you looking to do?" and you answered with React, GraphQL and SQL.
q: 这个问题在问什么，该怎么答？
q_en: What is this question actually asking, and how should you answer?
options: 在问方向：我想端到端 own 一个问题——从理解客户真正要什么，到做出来，到看它落地。
在问技术栈匹配度：把你最熟的语言和框架按熟练度排个序说一遍，方便对方对着 JD 上的要求打勾。
在问薪资和职级预期：先把你想要的层级和薪资范围说清楚，避免后面几轮浪费掉双方的时间。
在问你对岗位的了解程度：把 JD 上的职责逐条复述回去，证明你确实认真读过这份岗位说明书。
options_en: It asks for direction: I want to own a problem end-to-end — from understanding what customers actually need, to building it, to seeing how it lands.
It asks about stack fit: list your strongest languages and frameworks in order so they can tick them off against the JD.
It asks about pay and level: state your target level and range early so later rounds don't waste anyone's time.
It asks how well you know the role: recite the JD responsibilities back to prove you read the posting carefully.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Q["你接下来想做什么"] --> A["方向答案 — 端到端 ownership 离客户更近"]
  Q --> B["技术栈答案 — React GraphQL SQL"]
  A --> A1["给出可匹配的画像"]
  B --> B1["只重复了简历上已有的信息"]
tradeoff: 答方向 vs 答技术栈：列技术栈显得具体，代价是把一道「你要往哪走」的题答成了一份工具清单。
why: 这是方向题不是技术栈题。技术栈简历上都有；对方想知道我要往哪走，落点是 ownership 和离客户多近。
why_en: This is a direction question, not a stack question — the stack is already on my resume, so the answer lands on ownership and how close I get to the customer.
whenOtherWins: 只有当对方明确问「你主要用什么技术栈」时才列语言和框架，并说清哪些是主力、哪些是能上手。
optionMeanings: 当成职业方向题来答。
当成技术栈匹配题来答。
当成薪资与职级题来答。
当成岗位理解度测试来答。
optionMeanings_en: Treat it as a question about career direction.
Treat it as a stack-matching question.
Treat it as a pay-and-level question.
Treat it as a test of how well you read the JD.
optionDirectness: 对方问「你想做什么」这种开放句式时。
对方逐项念技术要求、在核对能力时。
对方明确说要先对齐薪资范围时。
对方问「你怎么理解这个岗位」时。
optionDirectness_en: When they ask an open "what do you want to do" question.
When they're reading requirements aloud and checking coverage.
When they explicitly want the range aligned first.
When they ask how you understand the role.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方拿到一个可以往下匹配的画像。
对方只知道你会什么，不知道你要什么。
把方向题答成谈判，顺序错了。
复述 JD 证明读过，但没回答你想要什么。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They get a profile they can actually match against.
They learn what you can do but not what you want.
Turning a direction question into a negotiation inverts the order.
Reciting the JD proves you read it but answers nothing about you.

q: 「你希望团队记住你什么？」这个收尾题的答案该长什么样？
q_en: What should the answer to "what would you want the team to remember you for?" look like?
text: 收尾题不能退回泛泛热情。给一个具体连接：我已经做过你们需要的两面——Meta 的 {{AI onboarding}} 和 TikTok 的{{规模化用户端界面}}——我不是来学这两样的。
text_en: Don't fall back on generic enthusiasm — leave a specific connection: I've already built both halves you need, the {{AI onboarding}} layer at Meta and the {{scaled user-facing product}} at TikTok.
why: 开放收尾题是礼物。没准备就会退回「我很期待努力工作」，那句谁都能说、转身就忘。会前先把这一句写好。
why_en: An open closing question is a gift, and without a prepared line I default to enthusiasm that anyone could say and nobody remembers.

q: VC 的 sourcing 电话，self-intro 该以什么句式收尾？
q_en: On a VC sourcing call, how should the self-intro close?
text: VC 是把你匹配到 3-5 家 portfolio 公司，不是筛一个岗位。收尾给三样可匹配材料：公司{{阶段}}、{{问题域}}、{{团队结构}}——说「我想做最早的工程师之一」，而不是「我在找一个做 X 的岗位」。
text_en: A VC matches you to three to five portfolio companies rather than screening one job, so close with three matchable inputs: company {{stage}}, {{problem domain}}, and {{team structure}}.
why: 单岗位口径 VC 用不上。给阶段、问题域、团队结构三个维度，他才能在 portfolio 里替我对号入座。
why_en: A single job title gives a VC nothing to work with, but stage, problem domain and team structure let them slot me against their portfolio.

scenario: Alma 那通 staffing 招聘人的电话，对方开场第一句是「I believe you have not sent me your resume, right?」——你是在通话过程中才把简历发过去的。
scenario_en: On the Alma staffing call the recruiter's opening line was "I believe you have not sent me your resume, right?" — you sent it during the call.
q: 这件事怎么根治？
q_en: What's the permanent fix for this?
options: 在通话里道个歉、马上补发一份，并解释最近面试太多所以漏掉了，态度诚恳一般不会造成什么影响。
把简历长期挂在 LinkedIn 个人主页上，让所有招聘人自己去下载，这样就不用每次都单独发一遍了。
接受面试邀请的那一刻就发简历，并在会前查一遍对方 LinkedIn、读完他发来的所有材料。
等对方在通话里主动开口要，再当场发过去——这样能确认发到对的邮箱，也顺便确认对方真的会看。
options_en: Apologize on the call, resend immediately and explain that too many interviews made it slip — sincerity usually smooths it over.
Keep the resume permanently on your LinkedIn profile so every recruiter can download it themselves and you never send one again.
Send the resume the moment you accept the invite, and before the call look the recruiter up on LinkedIn and read everything they sent.
Wait for them to ask on the call and send it live — that way you confirm the right address and that they'll actually open it.
tradeoff: 接 invite 即发 vs 会中补发：会中补发也能补上，代价是开场第一分钟在处理流程，而不是在听你说话。
why: 开场第一句用来补流程，等于白丢一分钟的第一印象。接受邀请那一刻就发，会前再查一遍对方 LinkedIn。
why_en: Spending the opening line on logistics burns a full minute of first impression, so the resume goes out the moment I accept the invite.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方明确说「简历先别发、我们走内部系统」，就按他的流程来，但仍要在会前确认他手上有你的材料。
optionMeanings: 会中补发并致歉。
改用 LinkedIn 自助下载。
接受邀请即发并会前做功课。
等对方要了再当场发。
optionMeanings_en: Resend and apologize during the call.
Let them self-serve from LinkedIn.
Send on accepting, and prep before the call.
Wait until they ask, then send live.
optionDirectness: 已经发生时的止损动作，不是预防。
对方是通过 LinkedIn 主动找到你时才够。
任何 recruiter 电话的默认流程。
对方明确说走内部系统时才成立。
optionDirectness_en: Damage control after the fact, not prevention.
Enough only when they found you through LinkedIn anyway.
The default process for any recruiter call.
Only valid when they said they use an internal system.
optionScenarioImpacts: 开场一分钟花在补文件上。
对方手上仍然没有你的 PDF。
对方带着你的材料开场，直接进内容。
把主动权交出去，还赌他记得要。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The first minute goes into chasing a file.

They open the call holding your material and go straight to substance.
You hand over control and bet on them remembering to ask.

q: 每次面试前至少 15 分钟要研究哪些东西？
q_en: What must the fifteen minutes of pre-call research cover?
text: 会前至少 15 分钟：公司{{官网}} + LinkedIn About + 一篇{{近期新闻}}；出门前确认三件——公司名{{会念}}、核心产品说得出、能点出一个竞争对手。
text_en: At least fifteen minutes before the call: the company {{website}}, their LinkedIn About, and one {{recent news}} item — then check you can {{pronounce}} the name, state the core product, and name one competitor.
why: 会念名字、说得出核心产品、点得出一个竞争对手——这三件是「为什么选这家」能成立的最低前提。
why_en: Pronouncing the name, stating the core product and naming one competitor is the minimum floor for a why-this-company answer to hold up.

scenario: 下一通是 recruiter 电话。过去几次的问题：简历没提前发、不知道对方是谁、开场没连接岗位、没准备实质问题。
scenario_en: Next up is a recruiter call. Recent misses: the resume went out late, you didn't know who they were, the opening didn't connect to the role, and you had no real questions.
q: 从接受邀请到通话开始，哪些是必须做完的？
q_en: Between accepting the invite and the call starting, which items are non-negotiable?
options: 接受 invite 的那一刻就把简历发过去，别等对方在电话里开口要。
在 LinkedIn 上看一眼这位招聘人是谁、在这家多久、之前做什么。
把公司的融资历史、投资人名单和历轮估值背下来，通话里主动抛出来。
花 15 分钟看官网和一篇近期新闻，并把两个实质问题写在纸上。
options_en: Send the resume the moment you accept the invite, instead of waiting for them to ask on the call.
Spend a minute on LinkedIn on who this recruiter is, how long they've been there, and what they did before.
Memorize the funding history, investor list and valuation at each round, and bring them up unprompted.
Spend fifteen minutes on the site and one recent news item, and write two substantive questions on paper.
why: 三件都是十五分钟内能做完的准备；漏掉任何一件，开场就得拿第一印象去补流程或补功课。
why_en: All three fit inside fifteen minutes, and skipping any of them means spending your opening on logistics instead of substance.
optionMeanings: 把发简历前置到接受邀请那一刻。
会前查清招聘人是谁。
背诵融资与估值细节。
官网加新闻，再写两个问题。
optionMeanings_en: Move sending the resume up to the moment you accept.
Find out who the recruiter is before the call.
Memorize funding and valuation details.
Site plus news, plus two written questions.
optionDirectness: 挡住开场那句「你还没发简历吧」。
分清内招还是第三方猎头，问法不同。
只有做投资尽调时才需要这些数字。
让「为什么选这家」有一个具体名词可点。
optionDirectness_en: It blocks the opening line "you haven't sent your resume, right?"
It tells you whether this is in-house or an agency, which changes what you ask.
Those numbers only matter when you're doing investment diligence.
It gives the why-this-company answer a concrete noun to name.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方开场就带着你的材料。
你知道该问岗位细节还是问客户名单。
背了用不上，还挤掉了产品研究的时间。
开场能点名产品，收尾有问题可问。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They open the call already holding your material.
You know whether to ask about the role or about their client list.
Memorized and unused, it also crowds out product research.
You can name the product at the open and have questions at the close.

scenario: Alma 那次问「为什么离职」，你的原话是：「团队在维护一个成熟平台，我想要 zero to one 或 one to ten 的经验来提升技术能力。」
scenario_en: Asked why you're leaving on the Alma call, your exact words were: "the team is maintaining a mature platform, I want zero-to-one or one-to-ten experience to enhance my technical skills."
q: 这句话的框架问题在哪？
q_en: What's the framing problem in that sentence?
options: 在措辞不够专业，「zero to one」是投资圈的黑话，应该换成「从头搭建一个系统的经验」。
在完全没有数字，应该说清那个成熟平台的规模，以及你负责的模块在里面占多大比例。
在贬低了现在的团队，维护成熟平台本身也很有价值，应该先肯定它再说自己想换方向。
在整句只有「逃离维护」，没有「奔向什么」——要说出我想去做成的那件具体的事。
options_en: The wording isn't professional — "zero to one" is investor jargon and should become "experience building a system from scratch."
There are no numbers — you should state the mature platform's scale and how large your slice of it was.
It disparages your current team — maintaining a mature platform has real value, so acknowledge that before pivoting.
The whole sentence is running away from maintenance with nothing to run toward — name the specific thing you want to go build.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Q["为什么离职"] --> A["逃离框架 — 平台成熟没意思"]
  Q --> B["奔向框架 — 想把一个问题做到上线"]
  A --> A1["对方只听到不满"]
  B --> B1["对方听到你要做成什么"]
tradeoff: 奔向 Y vs 逃离 X：说「在维护成熟平台」是真话，代价是整段只剩不满，对方听不到我要去做成什么。
why: 「维护成熟平台」是我在逃离的东西。框架换成奔向：我要把一个问题从第一个客户信号做到上线，并对结果负责。
why_en: Maintaining a mature platform is what I'm running from, so I reframe it toward what I want to build — a problem carried from the first customer signal to launch.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方直接追问「现在的团队具体哪里不合适」，那才正面说不满，但一句带过后仍要回到「奔向什么」。
optionMeanings: 问题归为用词太黑话。
问题归为缺少量化。
问题归为贬低了旧团队。
问题归为只有逃离没有奔向。
optionMeanings_en: Blames the jargon in the wording.
Blames the absence of numbers.
Blames it for disparaging the old team.
Blames it for running away with nowhere to run to.
optionDirectness: 对方明显听不懂创投术语时才成立。
在讲项目规模的那一段才需要数字。
如果你确实说了旧团队坏话时才成立。
整句只描述现状不满、没有去向时成立。
optionDirectness_en: Only holds if they visibly don't follow startup jargon.
Numbers belong in the project section, not here.
Only holds if you actually spoke badly of the old team.
Holds when the sentence describes dissatisfaction and no destination.
optionScenarioImpacts: 换个词，方向问题原样保留。
补上规模也还是在讲你不想要什么。
先肯定再转折，仍然没有目的地。
补上目的地，整句从抱怨变成计划。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: New wording, same missing direction.
Adding scale still only describes what you don't want.
Praise then pivot still arrives without a destination.
Adding the destination turns a complaint into a plan.

q: 「为什么离职」练到什么程度才算过关？
q_en: What is the pass bar for the "why I'm leaving" answer?
text: 过关标准：能作为一段独立的 {{30}} 秒陈述说出来，被{{打断}}后还能从中间接回去，并且离职原因和「为什么来这家」全程{{分开}}。
text_en: The bar: a standalone {{30}}-second statement, resumable mid-answer after an {{interruption}}, with the leaving reason and why-this-company kept {{separate}} throughout.
why: 标准不是「写好了」，是「被打断也能接回去」。达不到这个，下次一紧张又会回到「sorry, let me think about that」。
why_en: The bar isn't having written it, it's being able to resume mid-answer after an interruption — anything less and the next nervous moment brings back "let me think about that."
